hyps.why: A strong direct conv path makes extra conv capacity on edge 4 less valuable (diminishing returns).
A conv on the direct edge already supplies capacity, so edge 5's marginal benefit shrinks.
With edge 4 none, edge 0's signal reaches the output only via the longer 0->1->2->3 route, so a conv there is worth less.
With edge 1 absent, node 2 depends on the 0->1->2 route, so a strong edge 2 matters more.
With edge 0 already none, removing edge 1 leaves only the direct edge 3, so the loss is large.
Removing edge 5 hurts more when the direct edge is already none, since fewer routes to the output remain.
Edge 2's output cannot reach the output node when edge 5 is none, so the skip is useless.
Node 2 feeds only edge 5 to the output; if it is none, edge 1's conv contributes nothing to the output.
Edge 4 reads node 1, which is dead when edge 0 is none.
Removing edge 0 when edge 1 is also none cuts nodes 1 and 2 off from the input, leaving only the direct edge.
